dataset: NFL lines strategy framework — signal families and bet-type strategies
note: Research-based framework. Each signal and strategy is described with its inputs, the validation gates it must pass, and verified methodology sources. Signal implementations require the verified data feeds described in the Questions and Suggestions pages.

signal_families.name: Opponent-adjusted EPA ratings
signal_families.description: Expected Points Added per play, adjusted for opponent and weighted by recency, with a ridge-regression layer that controls how much model opinion may move the market number (out-of-sample weight, re-learned each run).

signal_families.name: DVOA / efficiency metrics
signal_families.description: Defense-adjusted Value Over Average compares every play to a league-average baseline in the same situation and adjusts for opponent quality; positive offensive DVOA and negative defensive DVOA indicate above-average performance. Used to test whether an EPA signal is sustainable or fragile.

signal_families.name: Success rate & efficiency composites
signal_families.description: Down-and-distance success rates (40% yards-to-go on 1st, 60% on 2nd, 100% on 3rd/4th) and multi-metric efficiency composites (EPA per play, down-set conversion) that smooth out explosive-play noise.

signal_families.name: Strength of schedule
signal_families.description: Forward-looking SOS built from Vegas win totals of opponents, which incorporate offseason movement, coaching changes, injuries, and roster development that prior-year records miss.

signal_families.name: Market-implied signals
signal_families.description: Convert each book's no-vig prices into implied margins and totals the market is pricing; use consensus and line movement as informational inputs (never as the sole edge).

signal_families.name: Injury-adjusted signals
signal_families.description: Adjust team and player ratings for absences, weighting starters over backups (Adjusted Games Lost methodology) and scoring the quality drop when 2nd/3rd/4th-string players replace starters on offense and defense.

signal_families.name: Luck-adjusted efficiency
signal_families.description: Strip luck from underlying performance: interception-worthy throws vs actual INTs, drops, fumble recovery rates, and DPI — producing adjusted efficiency that separates skill from variance.

bet_types.name: Single bets (spread / total / moneyline)
bet_types.description: One market, one leg. The most liquid, most efficient market — the cleanest test of a model's true edge. Model projection is compared to market price; an edge is flagged only when both edge and expected value clear the validation gates.

bet_types.name: Player prop bets
bet_types.description: Player-level totals (passing/rushing yards, TDs, receiving). Volume from recent games, efficiency pulled toward position average, adjusted for opponent defense and the team's implied points; a fitted distribution turns each projection into P(over). Props are the least efficient market, so the edge potential is larger but modeling must be rigorous.

bet_types.name: Parlay / combination bets
bet_types.description: Multi-leg combinations of spreads, totals, and props. Legs are priced jointly using a fitted distribution of real NFL results (extra weight on common margins such as 3, 7, 10) and the stored correlation matrix — never by naive multiplication of independent probabilities.

strategy_rules.name: Edge qualification rule
strategy_rules.description: A bet is flagged only when its edge clears the minimum threshold AND its expected value per dollar clears the minimum EV threshold. Thresholds are set in advance via validation gates and are not tuned to results.

strategy_rules.name: Grade-based screening
strategy_rules.description: Edge values are graded (e.g., >=2.5% ~ A, 0.5-2.5% ~ B, -0.5-0.5% ~ C, -2.5--0.5% ~ D, below -2.5% ~ F); only grades at or above the chosen cutoff are eligible.

strategy_rules.name: Selective skill-based deployment
strategy_rules.description: Strategies deploy only on games/markets where the composite signal is strongest; low-confidence games are skipped. Selectivity reduces variance and concentrates edge, making results measurable as skill rather than luck.
